claims.statement: The revised EU Waste Shipment Regulation and DIWASS entered into application on 21 May 2026, and prior-informed-consent procedures for notified waste are processed digitally.
Poland's GIOS provides DIWASS registration, test-system material, instructions, and API documentation, making a legitimate software integration route visible.
For covered Polish procedures, a notification is created through DIWASS, receives a unique identifier, and becomes visible to the authorities of dispatch, destination, and transit.

contrary_evidence: DIWASS itself is a public platform and GIOS publishes free instructions and API documentation, so form filling alone is not a durable product.
Poland has deferred some Annex VII digital handling to 1 January 2027, which may postpone a portion of near-term transaction volume.

economics.acquisition_route: Founder-led pilots with 3-5 Polish notifiers via environmental consultants, then referral/invite loops to carriers and destination facilities; no paid outreach assumed before a narrow proof
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Hypothesis: 150 European sites at 48000 PLN average ARR yields 7.2m PLN ARR; at 25% EBITDA, 4x EBITDA, and 80% founder ownership, business equity alone could exceed 5m PLN in years 5-7. Do not count retained earnings again; validate reachable site count and ACV.
economics.founder_time: 3-4 hours per day for a six-month validation build; cap manual review and hire a part-time waste-law specialist only after paid volume
economics.gross_margin_basis: Hypothesis: 78-88% at scale because software handles recurring checks, with human review reserved for novel classifications and exceptions
economics.payback: Hypothesis: 6-10 months on direct gross profit if one consultant channel yields 8-12 sites; validate sales-cycle length and API support cost
economics.pricing: Hypothesis: 2400-6000 PLN per operating site per month plus 30-90 PLN per executed shipment; validate against delay cost and current consultant spend
economics.retention_or_repeat: Shipment parties and facility details repeat, notification histories must remain auditable, and switching loses validated counterparties and route-specific error memory

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: A permissioned graph of verified operators, accepted routes, waste classifications, reusable guarantees, and authority error outcomes reduces setup time and false submissions for every subsequent movement
fingerprint.customer: Polish waste brokers, recyclers, recovery facilities, and carriers running notified cross-border waste movements
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Land through Polish environmental consultants and high-frequency waste carriers; each notifier invites foreign facilities and subcontractors, creating product-led counterparty spread
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Multi-party evidence workspace, DIWASS preflight, API handoff, and movement-status monitoring sold as a site subscription plus per-shipment fee
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The notifier or waste broker pays when opening an active notification and for each shipment executed under it
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A planned cross-border movement cannot proceed safely until all parties, documents, consents, and shipment identifiers agree in DIWASS

founder_fit: Strong match to data validation, workflow automation, and AI-assisted document extraction
Can be piloted part-time with synthetic and customer-provided packets before building a broad platform
B2B channel-led distribution limits constant networking and requires no public persona
Initial capital fits the founder's 100000 PLN limit
risks: Incorrect classification or a failed filing could delay high-value cargo and create professional-liability exposure.
Authorities or incumbent waste software vendors could provide sufficient native integrations.
Multi-party onboarding may stall if foreign receivers refuse another workspace.

structure.control_point: the validated DIWASS notification and multi-party handoff required before a notified waste shipment moves
structure.critical_dependency: reliable DIWASS/API interoperability and willingness of multiple shipment parties to exchange evidence through one workspace

thesis: Build a Poland-first transaction layer for cross-border waste brokers, recyclers, carriers, and receiving facilities that preflights a notified shipment, gathers each party's evidence, creates the DIWASS-ready packet, and monitors the movement through consent and receipt. The narrow wedge is not regulatory advice but preventing a truck from moving until the notification ID, route, parties, consent, guarantee, and facility acceptance reconcile. Distribution can be embedded through environmental consultants, hazardous-waste carriers, and recycling operators that repeatedly invite counterparties; every shipment adds reusable party, route, waste-code, and authority-response data. If the participant graph becomes the easiest way for counterparties to exchange verified details, the business can expand from Poland into a European waste-shipment trust network.
title: DIWASS Shipment Handshake Network
uncertainties: Number of Polish notifiers with enough recurring cross-border volume and poor enough current tooling to pay
Exact DIWASS API permissions, certification burden, and rate limits for a third-party service
Whether an invite loop can overcome counterparties' preference for email and existing ERP workflows
